criteria.description: Listed command past a fenced heading or beside a criteria-like heading is refused (T319-CR-1201)
criteria.non_member_fail: T320-CR-601 (bug 5, medium, Status New): a criteria section that holds an HTML block (<details>, <div>, <pre>, <table>), then a column-0 <!-- opener, then a fence holding `## y`, then the listed command, with a closing comment later in the document, answers none-named, exit 0, at head 650152741. The criterion says this document is refused. partsOf (finalise-rerun-at-head.js:325) opens a comment block at that opener, although Markdown opens none inside an HTML block, so the fence is not seen. The control with no later closer answers scan-broken. QA report 6:179 records it 4 of 4 on this head. The answer fails open: the criterion is not re-run, and nothing says so.
criteria.note: The recorded inputs hold. finalise-rerun-at-head.test.mjs:1246-1250 (refused past a fenced `## x` line, CRLF and `~~~` forms, and beside `## Rollback criteria`) and :1308 (T320-CR-501) run in npm test, .github/workflows/test.yml:58, on every PR; the test check passes on PR 949. The FAIL is T320-CR-601, an input inside the criterion's wording. Gate 6 is WAIVED with T320-CR-601/602/603 accepted by the owner at the loop limit. That waiver covers the QA gate. It does not amend the criterion: criteria-drift.js is clean. Gate 6's condition is 'T320-CR-601 fixed', and QA report 6:83 grades criterion 1 CONCERNS for this reason, so the caller has to reconcile the waiver with this criterion. The bug is not new (90aabca6c answers the same), but the criterion has no exception for that. T320-CR-603 goes the other way: a closed comment holding a fence marker, indented 1 or 3 spaces or in a list item, is refused as scan-broken (fails closed, low). The criterion does not say 'only when', so 603 is not a reason for this FAIL.

criteria.non_member_fail: command not named. QA report 6:95-113 records five runs of the four suites at 7cae65a14 (tree-equivalent to head: finalise-delta.js docs-only --base 7cae65a14 --head HEAD, reason tree-equivalent, exit 0), with load before and after each run. It names the suites but not the invocation that produced the per-test durations. The measured-criterion rule requires the command to be named. QA report 6's command list (line 200) holds only the full-suite test:remote run.
criteria.note: The prior non-member FAIL (re-measure: one run) no longer holds. QA report 6 has five runs, each with its 1/5/15-minute load (0.56 to 1.97), measured on 7cae65a14, tree-equivalent to head. The bound is met by a wide margin: the slowest test of the four suites has a median of 26.0 s and a maximum of 27.1 s, and that test is T319-CR-904/905, not new. The new SIGSTOP case (T319-CR-1303) has a median of 13.5 s and a maximum of 13.6 s. The fix is to add the command line (e.g. the §8 `command node --test …` over the four suites) beside the table in a committed record (the QA report or this DoD).
